metadata.note: cli-explainer spine, weekly work report, claude-hai channel. Episode 12, from the last pushed commit on chore/map-covers-repo (b425b19; origin contains it and the branch is in sync). FRAMEWORK: three questions for any index — DOES IT SAY WHAT IT COVERS / WHAT IS OUTSIDE THE DEFAULT SURFACE / DID YOU LIST IT OR CHECK IT. The purest statement of this series' recurring shape: every row accurate, and the document still misleading. B07 argues for the restraint of recording reviewed:false. Falsifiability beat is B08: all ten subsystem counts, the 1,005 total, the 97/95/2 recipe split and the 5 defects reproduce exactly, but the commit's '12 of 51 top-level paths' does NOT — I count 56 tracked top-level entries, 48 excluding dot-directories — so that ratio appears in no frame.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — composer, ask lands answered. Speaks the author's name.
beats.narration_text: I'm Uday Sonawane, and this is my week on Mycroft. The repository has a read-first map that tells an agent what is here. Every row in it was accurate. It was also missing ten entire subsystems — a thousand and five tracked files — and nothing in the file said it was partial.

props.segment: Uday Sonawane · Every Row Was True
output: none named by any Tier 1 file
recorded as listed, not as reviewed

beats.role_note: the premise — accurate and incomplete are not opposites
beats.narration_text: Here is the thing worth sitting with. Nothing in that map was wrong. Every path it named was real, every description was accurate, and that is exactly why it read as complete. A document that is entirely true can still mislead you, if what it leaves out is bigger than what it includes — and an agent reading it as its instructions would simply never have loaded a thousand files.

shot.show: every row true, and the map still incomplete
shot.visual_intent: Two bordered cards side by side. Left, in soft ink: 'every row accurate'. Right, in terracotta: 'and the map was partial'. Between them a crossed equals sign, drawn BETWEEN the cards and never through either label. Beneath, one line: nothing in the file said so.

beats.role_note: PROOF rubric — three questions for any index or map, AS A STRUCTURE first
beats.narration_text: Three questions for any index, map or manifest. One: does it say what it covers — because coverage is a claim, and a document that makes no coverage claim is not complete by default. Two: what sits outside the default surface — the paths your checks never walk. Three: did you list it, or did you check it — because those are different facts, and collapsing them is how an open question gets resolved by writing it down.
beats.new_visual_element: the three questions, as a numbered structure

shot.show: three numbered cards: DOES IT SAY WHAT IT COVERS / WHAT IS OUTSIDE THE SURFACE / LISTED OR CHECKED
shot.visual_intent: Three bordered cards land in a row, one per narration step. The third lands in terracotta — it is the restraint this commit shows and the one most likely to be skipped — and the rest of the reel is scored against all three.

beats.narration_text: The ask was to make the map match the repository, and to be honest about the difference between having listed something and having read it.

shot.show: the composer with the mapping ask

props.command: claude "classify every top-level path — and mark what has been listed but not reviewed"
props.segment: The ask · make the map fit the repo
output: list every tree, with tracked counts

beats.role_note: QUESTION 1 — what the map was missing, recounted from the tree
beats.narration_text: Question one. Ten subsystems, every one of them tracked, on disk, and the work of a named contributor. Projects, four hundred and thirty-five files. Case-study workflows, two hundred and seventy-seven. The verification layer, a hundred and fifty-four. Multi-agents, forty-one. And six more beneath those. A thousand and five files in total, none of which the map mentioned.
beats.new_visual_element: the ten subsystems and the total

shot.show: the four largest with counts, then the total of 1,005
shot.visual_intent: A vertical list of ten bordered rows, each with a path and its tracked count, the four largest in ink and the rest in soft ink. Beneath, a terracotta stat card reading 1,005, captioned 'tracked files the map did not mention'. Citation strip names the recount command.

beats.role_note: QUESTION 2 — the default surface, and what has never been walked
beats.narration_text: Question two, and this is the consequence. Not one of those ten directories sits inside the conformance checker's default paths. So the repository's own verify command has never once opened a file in any of them. And there is a second gap beside it: eight scoped instruction files sit below the root, outside the generated set, so the manifest check does not cover them either. Neither of those is a bug in anybody's code. They are both the same thing — a boundary nobody had drawn on the map.

shot.show: ten subsystems outside DEFAULT_PATHS, and eight scoped instruction files uncovered
shot.visual_intent: Two bordered panels stacked. The first: the ten subsystems, with a terracotta chip reading 'npm run verify has never reached them'. The second: eight scoped instruction files, with a chip reading 'outside the generated set'. Citation strip names the two mechanisms.

beats.role_note: ACTUAL-CODE LAW — the two failures found outside the surface, diagnosed and not fixed
beats.narration_text: Pointing the checker at those trees turned up exactly two failures, and the first one is ours. Three Kubernetes manifests are multi-document YAML, which is completely standard. Our checker calls the single-document loader. The files are fine; the defect is in the checker. The second is real and belongs to its own subsystem: a report full of bare not-a-number literals, which Python writes happily and JSON parsers reject.

shot.show: the loader mismatch and the NaN literals, with the verdict on each

props.title: two conformance failures, recorded and not fixed  @ b425b19
props.code:
# 1. three k8s manifests  -- multi-document YAML
   deploy/k8s/{infra,observability,pipeline}.yaml

   conformance.mjs:  yaml.safe_load(...)   # one document
   what it needs:    yaml.safe_load_all(...)
   -> the files are valid. the defect is in OUR checker.

# 2. congressional-signals/.../conformance_report.json
   "ticker": NaN          # python json.dump emits this
   JSON.parse -> Unexpected token 'N'
   -> a real defect, owned by that subsystem.
props.sparkLine: One of the two was ours

beats.role_note: QUESTION 3 — the restraint: listed is not reviewed
beats.narration_text: Question three, and this is the part I want to argue for. Every one of those ten is recorded with reviewed set to false. They have been listed. Nobody has read them against the constitution. Writing reviewed true would have felt tidier and would have closed the entry — and it would have resolved an open question by typing an answer into it. Listed and checked are two different facts, and a map that conflates them is worse than one that admits the gap.

shot.show: reviewed: false, and what writing true would have cost
shot.visual_intent: A bordered panel showing the recorded field with reviewed false in terracotta. Beside it, a second panel listing what the word reviewed would have asserted — read against SNICKERDOODLE, judged, accepted — each with a hollow unticked box, because none of them happened.

beats.role_note: the recount — everything reproduces except one ratio, which is therefore absent
beats.narration_text: I recounted all of it. The ten counts match the tree exactly, one for one, and they sum to a thousand and five. Ninety-seven recipes: ninety-five draft, two runnable-sample. Five defects, all in the same file. One figure did not reproduce. The commit says the old map classified twelve of fifty-one top-level paths; I count fifty-six tracked entries at the top level, or forty-eight if you exclude the dot-directories. Neither is fifty-one, so that ratio appears nowhere in this video.

shot.show: the ten counts and 1,005 verified; the 12-of-51 ratio not reproduced
shot.visual_intent: Left: four rows with drawn ticks — 1,005 summed, ten counts matched, 97 recipes split 95 and 2, 5 defects. Right: a terracotta panel on the one figure that did not reproduce, showing 56 and 48 against the claimed 51, and the line 'so it is not on screen'.

beats.role_note: the stale status file, and how the old content was preserved
beats.narration_text: One more thing was wrong and it was the file people read first. Status dot M D was tier one and five months stale — it still reported ninety-nine recipes and still listed the recipe lifecycle as an open question, which had been answered weeks ago. It is now refreshed against measured counts. The June snapshot was not deleted; it sits verbatim beneath the new content, and all twenty-four of its lines were verified present afterwards. Verify passes, nine hundred and ninety-three files conform.

shot.show: five months stale, refreshed, with the old snapshot kept verbatim
shot.visual_intent: Left: a bordered card showing what the stale file claimed — 99 recipes, lifecycle open — in soft ink with a terracotta cross beside it. Right: the refreshed figures, and beneath them a chip reading '24 of 24 old lines verified present'. A final chip: 993 files conform.

beats.role_note: scaffolded task — the rubric on the viewer's own index, with a GOOD/BAD discriminator
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Open whatever file tells a newcomer — or an agent — what your project contains. Then list the top level of the repository beside it and compare. Everything in the second list and not the first is invisible to anyone following your map, and it will stay invisible precisely because every line they can see is true.

shot.show: the composer with the handoff prompt and a GOOD/BAD discriminator
